claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

Firstly, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm looking to find out about claiming for my son Alex. He's 17 and lives with me here at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 17 years old (over 16), I need to ask a bit more about his current situation.

Is Alex currently in approved education (such as A-levels, Scottish Highers, or an equivalent full-time course) or approved training (such as a government-funded training programme)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's in sixth form doing his A-levels.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you for confirming that Alex is doing his A-levels in sixth form.

Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

Do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just one more question to confirm:

Is Alex currently working 24 hours or more per week, or receiving any benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, yes - he does work quite a bit alongside his studies. He has a part-time job at a local shop and works full-time hours there.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know about Alex's job. This is an important detail.

Just to clarify, when you say he works "full-time hours" at the shop alongside his A-levels, does he work **24 hours or more per week**?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - he works 24 hours or more per week at the shop.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Unfortunately, based on what you've told me, I have some important information about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Even though Alex is under 20 and in approved education (A-levels), the rules state that you'll **stop getting Child Benefit** if your child starts paid work for **24 hours or more a week** while in approved education or training.

Since Alex is working 24 hours or more per week at the shop, this would make you ineligible for Child Benefit for him, even though he's continuing his A-level studies.

Let me provide you with the formal eligibility outcome:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on my assessment, I'm afraid you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

### Summary

**Alex** – Not Eligible

Although Alex meets several criteria (he's under 20, lives with you in the UK, and is in approved education doing his A-levels), the fact that he works **24 hours or more per week** means you cannot receive Child Benefit for him. The rules specify that Child Benefit stops when a child starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week, even if they remain in approved education.

If Alex's working hours were to reduce to below 24 hours per week in the future while he continues his A-levels, you may then become eligible to claim Child Benefit for him again.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
